article-meta.article-title: Solving What Was "Lost to Time": How Audio AI and Primary Newspaper Scans Are Dating 76,000 Mystery Broadcasts
article-meta.kwd-group: OTR History, Audio AI, Primary Scans, Cultural Preservation

sec.title: A 70-Year Impasse in Broadcast History
sec.p: For over half a century, the Old Time Radio (OTR) community has lived with a persistent frustration: **thousands of surviving recordings have had no verified date or canonical identity.**
Generations of collectors copied reel-to-reel tapes, transcribed disc matrix codes onto paper notebooks, and traded cassettes stamped with labels like:

Even the most dedicated historians could only cross-reference what was written on physical labels or indexed in hand-typed logs. If a disc label was missing, the episode's true identity remained "lost to time."

sec.title: Why It Can Finally Be Solved Today
sec.p: For the first time in archival history, we have united the four essential pillars required to solve these mysteries at scale:
1. **The Comprehensive Master Archive**: 273,234 digitized historical recordings in our source-of-record catalog.

2. **Automated Neural Speech Recognition**: Local Whisper ASR transcribing entire half-hour broadcasts in seconds, extracting every character name, villain alias, sponsor commercial, writer credit, and local station chime.

3. **Millions of Primary Newspaper Scans**: Daily radio grids, *"Today’s Radio Highlights"* columns, and local station schedule pages from *The New York Times*, *Los Angeles Times*, *Chicago Tribune*, *Detroit Free Press*, *San Francisco Chronicle*, and regional dailies across America.

4. **Authoritative Master Network Logs**: Master episode logs compiled by Jerry Haendiges (`jjonez`), J. David Goldin's lifelong radio database, and trade periodicals (*Broadcasting*, *Billboard*, *Variety*, *Radio Mirror*).

sec.title: The "Smoking Gun" Method
sec.p: The breakthrough comes when internal audio clues meet contemporary print verification:

``` [Spoken Audio Clue] ───➔ [Character / Sponsor / Station ID] │ ▼ [Master Radio Log] ───➔ [Potential Air Date Window] │ ▼ [Morning Newspaper Scan] ➔ [Exact Station, Time Slot, and Highlight Blurb] │ ▼ ╔═══════════════════════════════════╗ ║ 100% CANONICAL HISTORICAL MATCH ║ ╚═══════════════════════════════════╝ ```

sec.title: Example: The "Lost" Gunsmoke Blood Feud
sec.p: For 70 years, a classic *Gunsmoke* recording circulated among collectors as an undated mystery labeled *"Ambush at Medicine Lodge"*.
sec.list: - **Audio Clue**: Our ASR transcription caught Matt Dillon mediating a blood feud between the Peavey and Cade families in the Gypsum Hills, followed by a CBS promo for the television program *Mr. Citizen* (hosted by Allyn Edwards in spring 1955).
- **Newspaper Proof**: April 16, 1955 newspaper radio grids confirmed the broadcast of **"The Gypsum Hills Feud"** (Episode #157).

sec.title: A Permanent Record for the Public
sec.p: Every resolved broadcast is immediately restored in our catalog, added to its exact day in the 365-day calendar (`/catalog/{month}-{day}`), equipped with synchronized WebVTT captions in R2, and durably recorded in our public progress ledger.
We are turning thousands of forgotten recordings into an open, searchable, and dated record of 20th-century cultural history.
